name: GEE, the Hon. Andrew Robert

headline.note: Gee's private legal work and family licensing business are documented, but available evidence does not establish hours, leave or complete date boundaries. Seniority and professional practice do not prove substantive full-time status. Study, party activity and elected office are excluded; missing evidence is not zero.

career_spells.evidence_note: Gee's federal first speech identifies Sydney University and St Paul's College; his NSW inaugural speech says he studied economics and then law. The secondary biography reports Bachelor of Economics (Honours) and Bachelor of Laws degrees. Enrolment and graduation dates, load and employment overlap are unresolved. College alumni account dated5May2025 supplies BEc(Hons) completion1991 and LLB1994, and residence at St Paul’s1987–90. Combined study end is therefore1994 at year precision; first enrolment remains unknown. College residence years are not silently equated with the whole degree interval.
career_spells.counting_note: Study is excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.evidence_note: Both inaugural speeches say Gee commenced life as a solicitor before moving to Asia with his brothers. Employer, admission and employment dates, hours and continuity are not identified.
career_spells.counting_note: Private legal employment is supported, but no countable full-time interval is established.

career_spells.employer: Wave Licensing International (family business; exact incorporated entity unresolved)
career_spells.role: Co-founder/operator in Hong Kong; reported director
career_spells.evidence_note: Gee describes a licensing business with brothers David and Matthew, operating from Hong Kong and Singapore. The brothers company biographies name Wave Licensing International, founded in 1996; a public indexed SCMP excerpt dated 3 December 1998 names Andrew as its Hong Kong director and Matthew in Singapore. Identification is supported by the matching people, business and locations; exact incorporated entity and Andrew ownership/appointment dates require corporate records. ABC 2015 corroborates return to Australia in 1999, but return is not proof of business cessation, so the former 1999 end field is now null. Company founding is not silently used as his employment start. Hours, remuneration and breaks remain unknown.
career_spells.counting_note: Private self-employment is supported, but the incomplete dates and unknown hours do not support an exact total.

career_spells.evidence_note: Gee identifies Colin Biggers & Paisley as his first solicitor role after returning to Australia and describes litigation work there. The secondary biography places the return in 1999; the frozen record and speeches place call to the bar in 2003. Exact appointment and departure dates, hours and leave are unresolved. ABC 2015 directly corroborates the 1999 return and 2003 Bar chronology. These remain contextual year-level bounds, not precise employment appointment dates.
career_spells.counting_note: Private employment is supported, but year-level boundaries and unknown substantive full-time status prevent calculation.

career_spells.employer: Self-employed barrister; Selborne Chambers then Queen's Square Chambers
career_spells.role: Barrister in civil litigation and family law
career_spells.evidence_note: The frozen occupation extract gives barrister from 2003 to 2011. Gee says he was called to the bar in 2003, read at Selborne Chambers, then joined Queen's Square Chambers and remained a member after moving to Orange; he says he practised in Orange and Sydney until the 2011 NSW election. Exact admission, reading, chamber and cessation dates, practice entity, hours and leave are unresolved. Contemporary ABC 2015 profile places the Orange relocation in 2005; this marks a location change within the practice, not a new employer or additional overlapping duration.
career_spells.counting_note: Private self-employment is supported, but year-level dates and unknown hours do not establish a substantive full-time interval.

career_spells.evidence_note: The NSW inaugural speech confirms election in March 2011; the federal speech describes five years in NSW Parliament. The secondary biography, citing parliamentary and electoral records, gives service from 26 March 2011 until resignation on 30 May 2016.
career_spells.counting_note: Elected office is excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.employer: National Party of Australia — NSW and federal organisations
career_spells.evidence_note: Gee's speeches document National Party membership and campaigning; the secondary biography records NSW endorsement in 2010, federal preselection on 30 April 2016 and resignation from the party on 23 December 2022. Membership commencement, campaign remuneration and any separate party employment are unresolved; parliamentary service is recorded separately.
career_spells.counting_note: Party activity is excluded under the codebook and is not assumed to be employment.

career_spells.evidence_note: The frozen roster and biographies establish House service from the 2 July 2016 election. Ministerial and committee offices are nested within elected service; he has sat as an Independent since leaving the Nationals on 23 December 2022.
career_spells.counting_note: Elected office is excluded under the codebook.

research_notes: The official occupation line starts with barrister practice in 2003; Gee's two inaugural speeches identify earlier solicitor and self-employed business work, recorded separately without invented dates.

The 1999 return and exact state-service endpoints come from a secondary synthesis tied to cited contemporary and parliamentary material; they remain follow-up targets for direct primary corroboration.
Chamber membership identifies professional affiliation, not an employer or proof of full-time work.
The interval between resignation from NSW Parliament and the federal election is not classified as paid employment; candidacy and campaigning are recorded as party activity with remuneration unknown.

Follow-up 2026-10-01: identified the previously unnamed Asian business as Wave Licensing International using the matching family/company biographies and a contemporary indexed director statement. Exact corporate entity/ownership and operational dates still need primary records; the direct SCMP page was inaccessible (403) and the public indexed excerpt is explicitly distinguished from a full-text read.

Searched named brothers and licensing business, former solicitor/chambers profiles, bar/employer records and full-time terms. No initial law firm, admission day, hours, leave or complete business appointment interval established. Reject same-name British architect/tribunal member, Cambridge academic, Macquarie executive and rugby player; do not assign the brothers later Wave Entertainment, Disney, coffee or CBD College work to Andrew.

Next avenues: corporate/public trade records for Wave Licensing International in Hong Kong and Singapore; contemporary CBP and NSW Bar directories for appointments; chamber records and employment/leave evidence. The 1996 founding and 1999 return provide leads, not a manufactured full-time interval.

Second follow-up2October2026 adds directly supported qualification years: economics honours1991, law1994, and college residence1987–90. These narrow the chronology without assigning an initial solicitor employer or extrapolating professional work from graduation.

Targeted1992/1993/1994 solicitor, bar-admission, full-time and Wave business searches yielded no new personal hours or employment boundaries. Same-name UK architect/tribunal member and US lawyer excluded. Existing SCMP access restriction respected; no archive opened to bypass it.

University Sydney Law School Report1993 vol2 no3, pp28–29, names an Andrew Gee as Law Society president; the study chronology fits but a clear person-level corroboration is still needed before adding student governance. Public report was recovered by direct download after web reader400 content-size limit. Next lead: student association historical office-holder list plus archived professional admission/employer records.

Follow-up3October2026 tested the specific1993 Sydney University Law Society presidency lead with SULS, student-president and full association-name queries. Only the already located university report established the name; no independent link to this member obtained. Hong Kong1994 and Wave Licensing searches returned existing commercial profile/press references and unrelated namesakes. Archived SCMP result not opened to bypass original restriction. No material fact or new employment term adopted; retain the student-governance lead until person-level corroboration is available.

Fourth follow-up4October2026 used exact solicitor, Colin Biggers & Paisley, chambers and Wave Licensing queries. Official first-speech and contemporary indexed results repeated the known sequence: return to Australia1999, CBP, bar from2003, Queen's Square practice and Wave directorship observation in1998. The surfaced archive copy of the restricted SCMP page was not opened or used to bypass source controls. No admission day, original appointment record, hours, leave or earlier solicitor employer emerged; same-name Macquarie executive and rugby player were excluded. No material change.
